==='''Brandon's Wheel of Time Reread on Twitter - 11/12 January 2011'''===

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24913758929289216 Brandon on Twitter - 11 January 2011]
I'm now onto the last part of EotW. I've mentioned before that I, personally, find this the roughest part of the entire series.

[http://twitter.com/FelixPax/status/24924117799014401 Felix]
Worse than books between LoC & WH? Really?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24924991271211008 Brandon]
Yes, honestly. I've mentioned before I don't have the problem with those that others do.

[http://twitter.com/dovijoel/status/24918705347502081 Dovi Joel]
Do you mean roughest as in not well written? I love that part, I find it so epic (especially when the Creator talks to him).

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24920626179350528 Brandon]
None of it is poorly written. In fact, some of the scenes--such as the ways--are wonderful.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24920715417358336 Brandon]
It's just that it seems like we have a different book, with different goals, starting on us here.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24914619055210496 Brandon]
The climax for EotW doesn't completely click for me. I like the Ways, I like the Blight, but the entire package feels too sudden.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24915279494520832 Brandon]
We spend the entire book with Tar Valon as our goal and Ba'alzamon as villain. Now, the Eye is the goal and two Forsaken are villains.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24915942869835776 Brandon]
Personally, I think this is due to RJ planning books 1-3 as one novel, then discovering it was too much and creating a break-point.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24918014864400384 Brandon]
To be fair, I feel I had some of the same problems at the end of Mistborn. Powers manifest that I could have foreshadowed better.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24918394776068096 Brandon]
One of the great challenges as a writer, particularly in fantasy, is to learn that balance of foreshadowing vs. pacing.

[http://twitter.com/Bonzi777/status/24919081626902528 Bonzi]
And I would think, foreshadowing effectively vs. giving away too much.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24920770970918912 Brandon]
Yes, exactly.


[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24923041943261184 Brandon]
For those curious, I'm reasonably sure books 1-3 were one novel at first. Tom D., CEO of Tor, told me in detail of RJ's WoT pitch.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24923369065422848 Brandon]
He pitched a trilogy, but the first book ended with Rand taking the sword (that wasn't a sword) from the Stone (that wasn't a stone.)

[http://twitter.com/gmreynoldsjr/status/24923936022073344 G. Michael Reynolds]
The sword in the stone!!! How on Earth did I miss that? :shame:

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24924505428201474 Brandon]
Lol. I missed it the first time too. And things like Caemlyn, Egwene, Gawyn, Galad, Merrilin. I at least got Artur Hawkwing...

[http://twitter.com/gmreynoldsjr/status/24925063488737280 Michael]
Ever feel like RJ removed any possibility of borrowing from any mythology ever again? He seemingly hit 'em all buffet-style.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24931414864560128 Brandon]
Actually, I've felt that very thing.

[http://twitter.com/feelieking/status/24924571215859712 James Powell]
I'd heard that one reason that WOT is so long is that Tor asked RJ for "more books", and he thought they meant "more WOT".

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24928650700783616 Brandon]
That's not actually true, from what I know. Tor never pushed RJ for more books. He was allowed to what he wanted, as he wanted.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24929695665496066 Brandon]
People are noting GRRM expanded ASOIAF also. RJ and GRRM are similar types of writers: http://bit.ly/e59ox0 Search for 'gardener.'

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24932296729567232 Brandon]
I'm am more of an architect than a gardener. I do more 'gardening' on character, but I plan world and plot very extensively.

[http://twitter.com/FelixPax/status/24931313173667840 Felix]
Did RJ have a cluster of concepts, themes or concepts written down in his notes? Mindmaps? To create his story's "garden"?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24946503105650688 Brandon]
Yes, many.


[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24952382978793472 Brandon]
You know, Lan's backstory is a lot like Superman's.

[http://twitter.com/HBFFerreira/status/24970258041274369 HBFFerreira]
Isam = Bizarro?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24972200608006145 Brandon]
Lol.

[http://twitter.com/sleepinghour/status/24953758983135233 sleepinghour]
Does Lan still have the locket from his mother? It was never mentioned again after TEoTW.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/24956652406968320 Brandon]
That is an excellent question.



[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25292312015806464 Brandon on Twitter - 12 January 2011]
"I'd like being your Warder." Rand to Egwene, near the end of EotW.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25295593127550977 Brandon]
It's interesting to see how much Loial adds to these scenes. His personality is a balancing factor; calm, knowledgeable, not arrogant.

[http://twitter.com/elektrotal/status/25295736987979776 Shivam Bhatt]
And yet, Loial disappears in the end game. Please bring him back for the finale!

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25296583750844416 Brandon]
The Wheel Weaves as the Wheel Wills, and I do as I must.

[http://twitter.com/Kyle2123/status/25292781933039617 Kyle West]
Is it hard for you to still enjoy the series now that you are "behind the scenes"?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25295714850443264 Brandon]
I think I enjoy it more, now, actually. Though I am a little sad not to be able to read new WoT books when everyone else does.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25299819635408896 Brandon]
Reading about the Green Man makes me think of the Jordancon costume contest. Look for him in these pics: http://bit.ly/fovZdi

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25302789282340864 Brandon]
One of the Forsaken attacks Lan. Nynaeve's response: Charge in with a knife. That always amused me.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25303196184346624 Brandon]
Also, the foreshadowing in this sequence is brilliant. The Green Man speaks of things that become important thousands of pages away.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25311731181944834 Brandon]
No, I'm not going to tell you what the VOICE at the end of EotW was. Lots of people like to ask, though.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25318550025543680 Brandon]
Rand, at the end of Eye of the World. "Oh, I won't ever touch it again. Not if I have to cut my hand off, first."

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25319011684188161 Brandon]
The book ends with a short Moiraine viewpoint. That makes four VPs in this book by my count. Rand, Nynaeve, Perrin, Moiraine.

[http://twitter.com/JeffEdde/status/25313913448955904 Jeff Edde]
Can Rand channel Light & Power as a result of touching the EotW, or does he have access to it because he is who he is?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25319337615167488 Brandon]
It was the power in the Eye, so far as I know.



'''''Non sequituri'''''

[http://twitter.com/SomniumMortis/status/25276334716489728 Thomas Grossnickle]
What philosophies have influenced WoT? I feelt a bit of the Hindu Creator, Preserver, & Destroyer ...

[http://twitter.com/SomniumMortis/status/25276496700514304 Thomas]
...with LTT an avatar of preservation and Rand the Destroyer...

[http://twitter.com/SomniumMortis/status/25276651734564864 Thomas]
Who destroys the world when it is beyond preserving, only to create it anew.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/25293195139096576 Brandon]
I see a lot of that too. I'm convinced RJ blended something from most major philosophies and mythologies into the books.
